issues.description: The problem statement gives conflicting instructions about the SealSaloon.stock attribute: one section describes it as a per-instance final Stock initialized in the constructor, while another section explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances). This contradiction (instance-final vs static) will confuse students about whether to implement stock as an instance field initialized in the constructor or as a static shared field. The solution implements a static final stock, which matches one part of the description but contradicts the earlier instruction to initialize it in the constructor as an instance field.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: either require a static (shared) stock (and remove the instruction to initialize it in the per-instance constructor), or require a per-instance final stock (and remove the requirement that stock be static). Update the problem text to clearly state the intended choice. If the intended design is a shared stock, state that stock should be declared 'private static final Stock stock' and initialized at declaration or in a static initializer; if it's per-instance, remove the 'static' requirement and instruct students to initialize it inside the no-arg constructor.

issues.description: The problem statement requires calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to be static (shared behavior using the shared stock), but the provided solution implements calculateTotalPrice as an instance method. This mismatch between the specified method modifier (static) and the solution's instance method may confuse students about whether to declare the method static or not.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the specification and the example solution: either change the problem text to allow calculateTotalPrice to be an instance method (since it accesses the shared static stock) or modify the solution to declare calculateTotalPrice as static. Prefer explicitly stating which form is expected (e.g., 'public static int calculateTotalPrice(Meal)') so students know the required modifier.
